rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who ostentatiously display their deeds do so so that people will praise them.
rows.anchor: يرون الناس أعمالهم ليروهم الثناء عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-maʿūn can mean the obligatory alms (zakāt).
rows.anchor: منع الزكاة التي هي قنطرة الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-maʿūn can also mean things customarily lent for use.
rows.anchor: الزكاة أو ما يتعاور في العادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa in the woe passage is consequential: neglect of the orphan already shows weak religion and deserves blame, so heedlessness of prayer, ostentation, and withholding zakāt merit it even more; prayer is religion's pillar, ostentation a branch of unbelief, and zakāt Islam's bridge.
rows.anchor: فالسهو عن الصلاة التي هي عماد الدين والرياء الذي هو شعبة من الكفر، ومنع الزكاة التي هي قنطرة الإسلام أحق بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the fa can mark causation, meaning, “So woe is theirs.”
rows.anchor: أو للسببية على معنى { فويل } لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them “those who pray” in place of a pronoun signals their bad treatment of both the Creator and other people.
rows.anchor: وإنما وضع المصلين موضع الضمير للدلالة على سوء معاملتهم مع الخالق والخلق

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that whoever recites Sūrat Araʾayta is forgiven if he pays zakāt; Bayḍāwī gives no grading.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة أرأيت غفر له أن كان للزكاة مؤديا
